headline: Rising energy costs from AI data centers land hardest on lower income, rural households, study finds
claim: Rising energy costs tied to AI data centers fell hardest on lower-income and rural households.
notes: published the week of 2026-11-09 (article says 'published this week'; page last updated 2026-11-10, no original date shown). Cornell-led study in Nature Energy, peer-reviewed academic work; no advocacy affiliation shown, but the researchers recommend policy changes. Grid-spending figures for 2020-2025 read as data analysis. The 76% larger rural/lower-income cost increase and the ~20% Bay Area wholesale-price estimate are not clearly labeled measured vs modeled.

headline: Two surveys find nearly two-thirds of teens use AI chatbots; some uses linked to worse mental health
claim: Young people who use AI chatbots during emotional distress have worse mental health and more suicidal thoughts and attempts.
notes: published 2026-10-30. Both surveys from advocacy groups, not academic institutions: JED Foundation (mental health group; 5,500 US students aged 9-17) and Common Sense Media (online safety group; sample size not stated). Correlational; the researcher says the data do not establish that AI causes the problems, and the link may run both ways. Same study as the Futurism row logged 2026-11-06.

headline: Elvis Presley rights holders sue AI music generator Suno
claim: Training AI on copyrighted songs harms songwriters and the music industry.
notes: published 2026-11-09; Elvis Presley Enterprises filed the suit 2026-11-06 in N.D. Cal., alleging Suno profited from Presley's music and likeness under Tennessee's ELVIS Act. Suno's profits 'believed to exceed $50 million'; damages to be proven at trial. Allegations only; no court has ruled. Plaintiff is a rights holder (interested party).

headline: Report warns AI bubble is 'primed to pop' and could hurt working people
claim: The AI investment boom is a financial bubble that could harm working-class Americans when it bursts.
notes: published 2026-10-21 (page date). Report 'Brace for Impact' by Open Markets Institute and Americans for Financial Reform Education Fund: advocacy groups with a stated policy position (interested party). Forecast of a crash, not a measurement of current harm. Same report as the Asia Times row logged 2026-11-05.

headline: AI-driven layoffs are creating a new class of boomerang employees
claim: Employers replaced workers with AI, then asked some of them back, with regret over AI-linked cuts.
notes: published 2026-10-30. SHL survey run by Propeller Insights, June-July 2026, more than 1,000 US and 1,000 UK workers. SHL is a commercial talent-assessment firm (interested party). The article reports employers asking workers back; the 'pulled the plug too quickly' view is an SHL executive's opinion, not a survey finding. Same survey as the Breitbart and People Matters rows.
